chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

In the case of a mukatab who pays half of his manumission contract and the half remains upon him, so he calls his masters and says: 'Take what remains as a single payment,' he said: 'They take what remains and he is freed.'

key_terms.مَوَالِيَهُ: His masters (plural of mawla in the context of ownership).
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: A slave who has entered into a contract of manumission in exchange for a specified payment.

ai.seo_question: What happens if a mukatab pays half his manumission fee and then offers to pay the rest in one go?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the masters are obligated to accept the lump-sum payment for the remaining half of the mukatab's contract, ensuring immediate emancipation rather than allowing them to delay or demand further installments. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle of facilitating the slave's freedom, reflecting the Quranic encouragement of manumission. It highlights the balance between the contractual rights of the master and the imperative of liberating the slave as quickly as possible.
